title: Accounts Assistant

12 Month Fixed-Term Contract

Location: Coventry

title: Construction Quality Administrator
description:
Construction Quality Administrator

Location: Based in Coventry (CV4) 3 days a week, and out on site 2 days per week
Salary: £27,000 per annum + £3,000 car allowance + Excellent Benefits
Contract& Hours: Full-time, Permanent 37 hours per week, Monday to Friday
Benefits: Enhanced pension contributions, Employer-paid Healthcare Cash Plan, Enhanced Maternity Pay, Employee Assistance Programme, and support for CPD

Must have a full UK driving license

Sustainable Building Services (SBS) is a multi-award-winning retrofit decarbonisation solutions provider and principal contractor delivering at scale across all housing tenure types social, owner-occupied, and private rental homes.

As a leader in residential decarbonisation, energy efficiency, and whole-house retrofit, we currently manage and deliver over £100m+ large-scale retrofit schemes, blending funding across mixed-tenures to maximise positive impact across communities.

Our work directly improves the living conditions, health, comfort, and wellbeing of thousands of households each year helping to reduce fuel poverty and address four of today s greatest challenges: the cost of living, energy security, climate change, and public health.

The Role: Quality Administrator

We are looking for a Construction Quality Administrator to support the delivery of our retrofit and energy efficiency projects by taking ownership of evidence population and lodgement preparation.

You ll play a key role in liaising with contractors, site teams, and coordinators to request, collate, and prepare all documentation required for Energy Efficient Measures in line with PAS 2030:2019, PAS 2035:2019 & PAS 2035:2023, and MCS Standards.

Working closely with Retrofit Coordinators, Regional Compliance teams, and subcontractors, you ll help ensure every submission meets our high compliance standards and contractual deadlines.

Key Responsibilities
- Collate all necessary paperwork for the installation of energy efficiency measures in accordance with PAS 2035:2019, PAS 2035:2023, and MCS requirements.
- Work closely with project Retrofit Coordinators to ensure all documentation is provided in line with contract programmes.
- Provide compliance support and guidance to regional delivery teams.
- Upload and manage documentation across designated platforms and shared locations.
- Maintain accuracy and attention to detail to ensure zero compliance failures.
- Meet all strategic partner contractual deadlines.
- Engage with sub-contractors to support compliant project delivery.
- Request client shared folder access and upload completed lodgement evidence post-project completion.
- Travel to other sites as required to provide hands-on administrative support.
- Take part in ad hoc projects or initiatives to meet evolving business needs.

About You

You ll be someone who thrives on accuracy, organisation, and teamwork, with a proactive mindset and a genuine interest in helping projects succeed.

Essential:
- Minimum 1 year of administrative experience.
- GCSEs and above.
- Strong IT skills, particularly Excel and Outlook.
- Excellent organisational and time management skills.
- Ability to work independently or collaboratively across multiple teams.
- Confident communicator with strong attention to detail.
- Ability to plan and meet tight deadlines.
- Full UK driving licence.

Desirable:
- Experience working within a geographically dispersed team using Microsoft Teams or similar tools.
- Customer service experience.
- A basic understanding of retrofit processes and standards.

Our Commitment to You

We are proud to be an equal opportunities employer. We believe in hiring the right person for the job and fostering a workplace where everyone is treated fairly and with respect, regardless of gender, age, race, family status, sexual orientation, disability, or religious belief.

Ready to make a difference one home at a time

Apply now and help us lead the way in sustainable building and energy efficiency.

No agencies please.

title: Credit Control & Accounts Receivable Administrator
description:
Credit Control & Accounts Receivable Administrator
Location: Coventry HQ / Hybrid
Salary: £26,000 - £28,000 DOE
Contract Type: Permanent, Full Time
Working Hours: 40 hours Monday to Friday, 0900 - 1730 with flex start/ finish
About the role
You'll be part of our Accounts Receivable team, helping customers pay on time, reducing overdue debt and keeping customer accounts accurate.

You'll build relationships with customers and work with Operations to resolve payment queries, disputes and retentions. Alongside collections, you'll handle daily cash posting, payment allocations and customer refunds.

Key responsibilities

Contact customers by phone and email to collect overdue payments and follow up on payment promises.
Post customer receipts daily, allocate payments to the right invoices in Summit, and record any retentions, short payments or allocation queries so they get followed up.
Send payment reminders and follow the agreed debt escalation process.
Log disputes in the AR database and work with customers, contract managers and Operations to resolve them.
Prepare for and attend weekly debt reviews with Operations, providing updates and following up agreed actions.
Track payment plans and support settlement proposals, getting approval in line with company policy.
Process customer refunds accurately, with the required approvals.
Escalate unresolved disputes, missed payment promises and collection risks quickly.
Keep clear records of customer contact, actions and agreements, and handle financial information confidentially.
Support the wider AR team and suggest practical ways we can work better.

What you'll bring

Experience in credit control, accounts receivable or a similar finance role.
Confidence having firm but friendly conversations about overdue payments.
Good organisation and the ability to prioritise a busy workload.
Attention to detail when posting cash, allocating payments and keeping records.
Clear written and verbal communication, and the ability to build good working relationships.
Confidence using Excel. Experience of Summit or a similar finance system would be helpful.
A proactive approach, willingness to learn and reliable follow-through.

Why join us?
As the UK's leading grounds maintenance and landscape creation provider, no two projects are ever the same - and neither are our people. That's why we're committed to nurturing a diverse and inclusive culture where everyone can thrive.

What we offer
- We offer career advancement and development opportunities through our bespoke apprenticeship programmes, our extensive in-house training academy, and coaching and mentorship.
- Join a diverse and inclusive workplace where you can collaborate with passionate and talented individuals.
- Contribute to projects that make a real difference in the community and environment.
- We recognise and reward your hard work with our wide-ranging benefits package designed to prioritise your wellbeing, support life choices, and help in both good and challenging times.

Benefits
- 25 days holiday plus bank holidays.
- Enhanced maternity and shared parental leave.
- Support for personal and professional challenges.
- Discounts on retail, holidays, gym memberships, and more.
- Secure your future - competitive pension scheme and resources to manage your finances.
- Colleague of the month and annual awards.
- Two days per year to support a cause of your choice.
- Comprehensive resources and support.

About our client
We are Europe's largest provider of grounds maintenance services and landscape creation, in the UK alone we're a community of over 3,000 passionate colleagues shaping the future of the green industry.

We understand what it means to grow. Our history dates back to 1919, and today, with a turnover of £250 million, we're more than just a company - we're a force for positive change. We offer a range of services to create, maintain, and manage landscapes across the UK.

Grow with us, and together we'll create a greener future for all.

If you receive suspicious outreach claiming to be from us, please contact us via the ManpowerGroup website.

title: Technical Customer Support Coordinator
description:
Technical Customer Support Coordinator

Location: Coventry
Contract Type: Permanent
Salary: 26,000
Hours: Full Time
Driving Licence Required: Yes
Own Car: Yes

About the Role

We are seeking a proactive and customer-focused Technical Customer Support Coordinator to join our growing team. This role is ideal for someone with strong customer service skills and a practical technical understanding of products, troubleshooting, fault diagnosis and customer support.

You will act as the first point of contact for customers requiring technical assistance, providing support and guidance on product installation, operation, assembly, maintenance and fault finding. Typical enquiries may relate to electrical supply issues, gas supply concerns, product assembly, product faults, replacement parts and general technical troubleshooting.

Working closely with internal departments, suppliers and service partners, you will ensure customer issues are resolved efficiently while delivering an excellent customer experience.

Key Responsibilities
- Providing technical support to customers via telephone, email and online enquiries.
- Diagnosing and assisting with product faults, assembly issues and operational problems.
- Advising customers on electrical and gas supply requirements, troubleshooting and safe product use.
- Supporting customers with assembly, installation and replacement part enquiries.
- Logging, tracking and managing customer cases through to resolution.
- Processing warranty claims and coordinating replacement parts where required.
- Maintaining accurate records using CRM systems and internal databases.
- Liaising with suppliers, service engineers, logistics teams and other departments to ensure customer issues are resolved promptly.
- Monitoring ongoing cases and providing regular updates to customers.
- Producing reports and assisting with general departmental administration.
- Supporting customer retention through professional and effective problem resolution.

About You

To be successful in this role, you will have:
- Previous experience within a Technical Customer Service, Technical Support, Product Support or Customer Care role.
- Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving abilities.
- Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal.
- A professional, patient and customer-focused approach.
- Good IT skills including Microsoft Word, Excel and Outlook.
- Experience using CRM or case management systems.
- The ability to manage multiple customer enquiries while maintaining attention to detail.
- Confidence explaining technical information to customers in a clear and easy-to-understand manner.
- A full UK driving licence.

Desirable Experience
- Experience supporting customers with consumer products, appliances, mechanical or electrical products.
- Experience handling warranty claims and replacement parts enquiries.
- Understanding of basic electrical and gas-related fault finding.
- Experience working within a manufacturing, engineering, retail or product support environment.
- Experience liaising with service engineers, distributors or field-based technicians.

title: Wellbeing Co-ordinator (12 Months FTC)
description:
An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Service User Wellbeing Co-ordinator to join our Domestic Abuse Service for a 12 month FTC to cover maternity leave. You will be joining a multi service charity based in Coventry. In return, we offer a competitive salary of £29,093 per annum, plus on-call payments and a contributory pension scheme. Annual leave 26 days + bank holidays with an additional day s leave for every 2 years of service up to a maximum of 29 days per annum. We also have a comprehensive in-house training programme.

What We Do:

The charity has a fully trained staff team providing Supported Accommodation and support to victims of domestic abuse. There is also an on-site Children s Nursery that provides full day care for pre-school children.

We are looking for a reliable and committed individual who is able to:
- Work closely with staff and Valley House domestic abuse service users to create a groupwork programme aimed at promoting positive health.
- To provide a range of groupwork and learning and development activities designed to support our service users to achieve positive health and wellbeing outcomes.
- Consult with staff and service users to identify a range of groupwork activities and interventions that will support service users to improve their health and wellbeing.
- Develop and deliver the programme across Valley House services.
- Identify and engage with partner agencies, leading to partners delivering groupwork activities for our service users as part of the programme.
- Monitor and evaluate the impact of the groupwork sessions, creating reports as and when required.
- Use the evaluations to continually improve the programme, using examples of good practice as appropriate.
- Support service users to co-deliver activities as appropriate.
- Be part of the on call rota.
- To provide 1-1 wellbeing support to service users.
- Promote and safeguard the welfare of children and vulnerable people that you come into contact with as part of your role.
- Ensure that Child Safeguarding and Safeguarding Adult Procedures are followed as necessary and to liaise with statutory agencies and attend inter-agency meetings as required.

The successful candidate will have:
- NVQ Level 3 in a related field and/or a minimum of 3 years relevant experience with survivors of domestic abuse.
- Experience of developing and delivering groupwork programmes.
- Experience of partnership working.
- Knowledge and understanding of health and wellbeing interventions and how to effectively promote them.
- Knowledge and understanding of the difficulties faced by survivors of domestic abuse.
- Knowledge of best practice in relation to safeguarding adults and children.
- Understanding and passion for the work of Valley House.
- Ability to work effectively within a team and on own initiative.
- Ability to work flexibly.
- Competent in the use of IT tools, including Word, Excel and Outlook.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Additional requirements:
- To take part in an out of hours on call rota with other staff.
- Be mobile and able to travel city wide at short notice (car driver with use of a vehicle).
- Candidates who are not car drivers, due to a disability, will be considered.

This post require a satisfactory DBS check.

This vacancy is open to women only (exempt under the Equality Act 2010 Schedule 9, Part 1).

The hours of work are 37.5 hours per week.

The closing date is Monday 14 December 2026 and interviews will be held on Friday 18 December 2026.

title: Booking Administrator
company: University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire NHS Trust
advertiser_name: University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire NHS Trust
description: We are looking to recruit 3 WTE Booking Administrators to provide comprehensive administrative, booking and customer service support to facilitate efficient access to outpatient services in accordance with Trust, departmental and national standards. Please be advised sponsorship is not eligible for this post. Closing Date: Please be advised that this job advert will close as soon as sufficient applications have been received. Please apply for this job as soon as you can, if interested. Interviews will take place week commencing 30th November 2026. The post holder will facilitate coordinating appointments, maintaining accurate patient records, communicating effectively with patients and clinical teams and supporting the effective utilisation of clinic capacity. The post holder will support the implementation of new and revised booking processes. As these processes become established, the role will evolve to focus on the ongoing administration, monitoring, maintenance and continuous improvement of standardised booking procedures, supporting consistent delivery and sustainable operational performance across the Trust. The role also involves supervision of the day-to-day workload of Band 2 booking support staff. The overall activities of the post-holder will include: Work effectively as a team member. Supervise the day-to-day workload of Band 2 booking support staff. Maintain spread sheets and databases including the production of regular information reports. Use own initiative to meet tight deadlines. Maintain accurate electronic filing systems. Ensure patient appointment information is up to date and accurate with continuous administrative validation using standard protocols. Coordinate, book, amend and cancel outpatient appointments using Trust systems and agreed booking procedures. Support the effective utilisation of clinic capacity by identifying vacant slots and liaising with the specialty team to assist with the management of appointment schedules. Liaise with patients regarding appointment arrangements and booking enquiries. Arrange interpreters, transport and additional services required to support attendance at appointments. Escalate booking concerns, clinic capacity issues and pathway delays to the appropriate teams and managers. Assist in reducing avoidable appointment waste through proactive administrative support. For further details of the role please see the attached Job Description.
